scope: Local ad-hoc signed Apple Silicon app; native Wails bridge and runtime-only installation. No model inference.
observations: Opened native Gemma Desktop.app with a new isolated private data directory.
Chat empty state, Models, Settings, and Harness Lab rendered through the native Wails bridge.
Installed mlx-serve-26.11.1 entirely in Models; durable job visibly advanced through extracting to complete without a terminal or model download.
Installed runtime remained inactive; Check model, Start runtime, and Use for chat remained disabled without an installed compatible model.
Settings continued to show External Ollama; personal model defaults were not promoted.
Harness Reliability showed frozen-arm, development-screen and fresh-qualification controls; inference controls were disabled without the required workspace and agent.
Right arrow moved focus from Reliability to Compare; Return activated the focused tab.
App remained running after window close, reopened with the same Harness view, and stopped after Quit.
Installed mlx-serve and completed installation job persisted across the final app rebuild and restart.
Final oMLX preview showed bundled package/no network transfer, private destination, 386.9 MB temporary space, 10.0 GB reserve, and 11.6 GB required free space.
Final E4B preview showed network download, private model destination, 4.8 GB temporary space, 10.0 GB reserve, and 19.6 GB required free space; preview was cancelled without downloading.
Final rebuilt app exited after Quit; no additional inference was run.

foundAndCorrected.issue: Install preview omitted the exact destination and temporary storage requirement, and described the bundled archive as a download.
foundAndCorrected.status: fixed; host preview and rendered tests passed; corrected runtime and model dialogs verified in rebuilt native app

limits: This is an existing development Mac using an isolated fresh app profile, not a clean physical machine.
UI model acquisition and runtime inference were not exercised; the separate oMLX/E4B manager probe supplies bounded live evidence.
No Developer ID signing, notarization, public distribution, coding-quality comparison or default promotion is claimed.
